summary: A construction contractor's receipts for labor and materials incorporated into a structure for the owner are not subject to retailers' occupation tax; the contractor owes use tax on its materials as their end user, so the owner pays no sales tax.

conditions.when: Furniture, area rugs or floor covering attached only with two-sided tape, drapes, trade fixtures, or portable appliances (stoves, refrigerators, washers) the contractor sells, even if installed under the contract

citations.title: 86 Ill. Adm. Code 130.1940(c) (Construction Contractors and Real Estate Developers)
citations.quote: A construction contractor does not incur Retailers' Occupation Tax liability as to receipts from labor furnished and tangible personal property (materials and fixtures) incorporated into a structure as an integral part thereof for an owner when furnished and installed as an incident of a construction contract.

citations.title: 86 Ill. Adm. Code 130.1940(a)(3)
citations.quote: "Construct" means build, erect, construct, reconstruct, install, plant, repair, renovate or remodel.

citations.title: IDOR ST 17-0017-GIL (June 2, 2017)
citations.quote: In Illinois, construction contractors are deemed end users of tangible personal property purchased for incorporation into real property.

notes: Covers improvement (incl. flooring) and repair: 'construct' includes repair, renovate and remodel. Floor coverings cemented or fastened with tacks, staples or tack strips are incorporated (130.1940(c)(1)); floating floors are not addressed and are unverified. A contractor may pass its use tax on in its price or as a 'reimbursement of tax', not as sales tax (ST 17-0017-GIL). Earliest dated text read is ST 17-0017-GIL. 2026-11-02: cited page moved from https://tax.illinois.gov/research/legalinformation/regs/section-130-1940.html to https://www.ilga.gov/commission/jcar/admincode/086/086001300S19400R.html.

summary: A delivery charge for goods that are exempt at that sale is not taxable: when all the property sold is exempt, the whole receipts including delivery are not taxable.

conditions.when: Exempt and taxable goods delivered together: the charge is exempt only if the exempt goods' selling price exceeds the taxable goods'

citations.title: 86 Ill. Adm. Code 130.415(b)(1)(F)(ii) (Transportation and Delivery Charges)
citations.quote: If the retailer determines that either the purchaser or all of the tangible personal property being sold is tax exempt, the entire gross receipts from the sale are not taxable, including the delivery charge.

citations.title: IDOR ST 17-0026-GIL (June 28, 2017)
citations.quote: then there is no inseparable link, and the delivery charges are not taxable.

notes: Before 2026 Illinois groceries were not exempt but low rate (1% state plus RTA/MED); their delivery charges, when inseparably linked, were taxed at the low rate (130.415(b)(1)(F)(iv)), which this code does not cover. From 2026, groceries are exempt from state tax but taxed by RTA/NITA, MED and local grocery taxes where imposed; there a linked delivery charge follows the grocery's local treatment, which is not 'exempt goods' in the code's sense. 2026-11-02: cited page moved from https://tax.illinois.gov/research/legalinformation/regs/section-130-415.html to https://www.ilga.gov/commission/jcar/admincode/086/086001300D04150R.html.

summary: A delivery charge for taxable goods is part of taxable gross receipts only when there is an 'inseparable link': the buyer could not get the goods without paying it (no pickup, no free-delivery option).

conditions.when: The seller offers no way to get the goods without the delivery charge (no pickup option, no free or qualifying free delivery), or the charge is not separately identified
The buyer could pick up the goods or had a free delivery option for the same item price, and chose paid delivery

citations.title: 86 Ill. Adm. Code 130.415(b)(1)(B)(i) (Transportation and Delivery Charges)
citations.quote: Outgoing transportation and delivery charges are part of the gross receipts subject to Retailers' Occupation Tax when there is an inseparable link between the sale of tangible personal property and the outgoing transportation and delivery of the property.

citations.title: 86 Ill. Adm. Code 130.415(b)(1)(B)(iii)
citations.quote: outgoing transportation and delivery is considered a service separate and distinct from the sale of tangible personal property that is being transported or delivered and is excluded from the gross receipts subject to the Retailers' Occupation Tax.

citations.title: IDOR ST 17-0026-GIL (June 28, 2017)
citations.quote: If property can only be obtained by paying transportation or delivery charges, then an inseparable link exists, and the delivery charges are taxable.

notes: Kean v. Wal-Mart Stores, 235 Ill. 2d 351 (2009). Applies to postage and carrier charges alike (covers the .mail and .carrier subcodes). A taxable delivery charge takes the rate of the goods (130.415(b)(1)(F)), so for low-rate food it is low rate. 130.415 (b) as amended effective 2016-04-01; earliest dated text read here is ST 17-0026-GIL. 2026-11-02: cited page moved from https://tax.illinois.gov/research/legalinformation/regs/section-130-415.html to https://www.ilga.gov/commission/jcar/admincode/086/086001300D04150R.html.

summary: Since September 1, 2009, candy is excluded from Illinois' low-rate food and taxed at the high rate: 6.25% state plus all local taxes.

citations.title: 35 ILCS 120/2-10 (Retailers' Occupation Tax Act, rate of tax)
citations.quote: Notwithstanding any other provisions of this Act, beginning September 1, 2009, "food for human consumption that is to be consumed off the premises where it is sold" does not include candy.

citations.quote: For purposes of this Section, "candy" means a preparation of sugar, honey, or other natural or artificial sweeteners in combination with chocolate, fruits, nuts or other ingredients or flavorings in the form of bars, drops, or pieces.

citations.quote: Candy is taxed at the State sales tax rate of 6.25%.

citations.quote: Alcoholic beverages, soft drinks, candy, and food that is prepared for immediate consumption are taxed at the regular sales tax rate of 6.25%, plus any applicable local taxes.

citations.quote: caterers;
